page0.text:
"I'm coming in, Sakura."
He opens the door without waiting for a reply.
He's never waited for his little sister to answer before opening the door.

page1.text:
"What, she still isn't back yet? What am I gonna do with her?"
He clicks his tongue and steps into the room.
Shinji Matou paces around his sister's room like a blind dog, running his nails along the walls.

page2.text:
"Sakura. Are you in the basement today, too? What are you doing down there without me?"
Nobody answers his repeated questions.
There's no one else in the room.
His sister hasn't been back home for the last few days.
Shinji keeps pacing around the room, even though he knows full well that its resident isn't here.

page3.text:
"You're always like that. Haha, you're seriously always like that!"
He picks up a clock and throws it.
The sound of the glass breaking irritates him more than he expected.

page4.text:
"Where'd she go? Keeping secrets from her big brother..."
He keeps throwing things, as if spitting out his anger.
...That's how this always goes.
It's how he's compensated on a regular basis for the last few years.
It's the greatest act of resistance he can do to forgive himself and his sister, ever since learning the truth three years ago.

page5.text: When he was born, the Matou bloodline had already outlived its purpose.

page6.text:
Their noble line lost its power, and the Matous were reduced to ordinary people.
Their only special assets were their knowledge.
A once great lineage of arcane scholars met its obscure end in the Orient.

page7.text:
He was told those facts, even as a child.
He was taught the Matous were special, a clan entrusted with miracles.
Were.
There were no Matous left who could use magecraft, and they would have to live in society as normal people from now on.

page8.text:
But he didn't think so.
It's true that without Magic Circuits or whatever they were called, he couldn't perform magecraft on his own.
He knew that the mages died out with his father's generation, and that he wasn't qualified to inherit the Matou name.
But the Matous still had records of their miracles.
Only their bloodline was over. They still had their wealth of knowledge.

page9.text:
To the boy, that was enough to make him special.
He wasn't like other people.
The Matous were a chosen people.
Their worth hadn't diminished just because they lost their magical power and stopped being mages.
He was proud to be part of that special family, and would live an exceptional life.
He might be lacking as a mage, but he was born into a chosen family, that was for sure.

page10.text:
...One day, a new child came into their fold.
His father said that the girl had no next of kin, so they would be adopting her.
It was more than ten years ago.
From that day forward, the girl named Sakura became his little sister.

page11.text:
At first, he didn't like her.
He didn't want some foreign element to come into their special family.
But as the days passed, he began to approve of her.
Sakura was quiet, plain, and little better than a guard dog.
Trying to be hostile towards her was a waste of time, so he began to dote on her stupidity, to an extent.

page12.text:
He buried himself in books, learned arcane arts that he couldn't perform, and thought of himself as the Matou heir.
Only he was allowed into the Matou library.
His sister was adopted, and she would never be chosen as the heir, so she had no right to look at those books.
Surely, she would live the rest of her life as a normal person, unaware of the Matous' remaining precious knowledge.
That notion satisfied his arrogance.

page13.text:
Each mage family only has one successor.
He knew that, so he never had any doubts that his sister would be cast off and raised separately.
Only one of them could learn magecraft.
So it was natural that he didn't see her around much.

page14.text:
That's right.
In fact, he pitied her.
They lived in the same house and had the same parents, and yet only he was considered special. He felt sorry for his sister who wasn't chosen.
His haughty attitude was the compassion of one who is superior, and of course, a source of his self-esteem as a reliable big brother.

page15.text:
So, the brother pitied his sister, and treated her with affection.
His sister never looked him in the eye.
He figured she felt ashamed of herself, and so he doted on his helpless little sister.
Until the day he learned the truth.

page16.text:
"Huh...?"
That was the only sound he could make when he happened upon that room.

page17.text:
A room he never knew about.
Wisdom that was never imparted to him.
And talents he was never born with.
All of that was here.
And she was in the middle of the room,
surrounded by black, squirming things and their scary grandfather.
His father glanced at him with a look of scorn he'd never seen before, as if he was an intruder.

page18.text:
It was over.
Everything he'd ever believed, that he'd constructed in his head, was turned upside-down.

page19.text:
He wasn't the special one.
His sister wasn't being kept away.
She wasn't the one to feel sorry for.
He wasn't the one looking down at her out of pity...

page20.text:
His life was transformed.
Now that his father didn't need to hide it anymore, he began to interact only with the little sister.
His little sister still wouldn't say anything. She just kept staring at the floor, like always.
With that same attitude that seemed like she wanted to escape his gaze, she said,
"...I'm sorry, big brother."
She said it with the same sympathy that he once directed at her.

page22.text:
He laughed.
He guffawed like there was no tomorrow.
It was so hilarious he wanted to break everything.
The girl he'd thought of as a plaything was the real master, while he was a clown all along.
Was he the crazy one, or her?
Probably both.
His life shattered, he went back to the house, and realized something.

page23.text:
It wasn't as if the world suddenly got turned around.
His environment was always this way.
The only one who had it backwards, who misunderstood, was himself.
He realized how wretched he was. He had it all wrong from the beginning.

page24.text:
The next three years were nothing but pain for him.
His father died, and his grandfather only paid attention to his sister.
Shinji Matou was no different from the air inside the mansion.
He was treated like it didn't matter whether he was there or not, and in fact, that's all he was worth.

page25.text:
And she sympathized with him.
She said, "sorry."
She didn't necessarily say it out loud, but she apologized every time they saw each other.
She apologized for taking Shinji Matou's place.

page27.text:
She should have just ignored him.
Then he would have lost his dignity, and he wouldn't feel any hope.
Sakura would apologize.
That only made him feel like there was no outlet for everything he was feeling.

page28.text:
"I'm your kind big brother."
"Your one and only brother you can count on more than anyone else."

page29.text: In light of his humiliation, surely there was nothing wrong with him treating her this way.

page30.text:
"Ha... Is she still at Emiya's place?
You're the family heir. Our heir! The great successor to the Matou line!"

page31.text:
The room shows no signs of being lived in.
That went without saying.
To Sakura Matou, her only "bedroom" was that underground nest, while this room was just for appearances.
She wouldn't care no matter how much he messed up the room or how many things he broke.
It won't change the fact that her name is the one on the door.

page32.text:
Argh, and you're still gonna apologize to me! It's always 'sorry' with you! If you're really sorry, then do what I tell you! You feel guilty? I don't care. If you think of yourself as a Matou at all, then you should be a good little sister and do what your brother says!
He tears off the bedsheets.
She belonged to him.
She never defied him, never thought for herself. She just lived here, so why did she leave him now?

page33.text:
"You...you took her from me, Emiya."
That was a miscalculation on his part.
He knew that she was attracted to Shirou Emiya.
Before they met, she never had any interests, but she started to think like a human being once she met Shirou Emiya.
Then, she gradually recovered her personality, until she left Shinji.

page34.text: After all the trouble he went through to act like a nice older brother, how could she go with that stranger Shirou Emiya, and not him...!?

page35.text:
"I told them so. I said that she shouldn't go to his house, but that geezer said some crap about keeping an eye on the Emiyas!"
Their grandfather never made any effort to bring Sakura home after giving the order.
He just said to let her be, and even warned Shinji to restrain himself.

page36.text:
"Just you watch. I'll pay you back for this, Emiya. I'll rip you apart while Sakura watches..."
...That's right.
If Sakura was going to leave him, then he'd just force her back into their old relationship.
If she was going to leave the Matou family for him...
